rule: The input is a strip of equal framed panels, and the last panel is the bare frame. Each object in the earlier panels changes from step to step by inserting the same block of rows or columns at a fixed index, or by translating. Its bounding box shifts by a constant offset each step. The output is the bare last panel with the next step of its own sequence drawn in. When two sequences with different colour sets alternate (period 2), the last panel continues the sequence that has its parity.
scope: Supported: vertical or horizontal strips of 3-6 panels, panel sides from 5 up to 30, constrained by the full strip fitting within 30x30, total size at most 30. Frames are random mirror-symmetric decorative rings of thickness 1-2 in one or two colours around a background interior. Each sequence has 1-3 target objects, each with 1-2 colours, built from a prefix, k copies of a block and a suffix. Objects grow along one axis by 1-2 rows per step, with along-axis drift -d, 0 or +d. Translating objects move by one cell in any of the 8 directions. Period-2 scenes with an interleaved distractor sequence are supported. Not supported: growth along both axes at once, perpendicular drift of growing objects, objects that appear or vanish mid-sequence, objects on frame cells, sequence periods above 2, and non-ring frame layouts. In random scenes, objects within one sequence have pairwise distinct colour sets; only the replayed test fixture reuses a colour set. Optional panel_height/panel_width and sequence_period controls are honored exactly. At least five panels are required for period 2.
constraints: Object cells lie only on background interior cells of the template and never use the background or frame colours.
The background is strictly the most frequent colour of the input grid.
A local reimplementation of the panel-period search (axis 0 first, smallest p, agreement on the last panel's non-background cells) must return exactly the intended axis and panel length.
Each object's colour set is identical in every state, including the output state. Within one random sequence, objects have pairwise disjoint colours.
Every state of every object is 4-connected and has a tight bounding box, so the latent position equals the bbox origin.
Within a panel, objects are separated by at least one cell in Chebyshev distance, so 4- and 8-connected components agree.
Every state, including the output state, fits inside the panel interior.
Period 1: all filled panels have the same content colour set. Period 2: consecutive panels differ in colour set, and panels two apart match; this needs at least 5 panels.
The first object of each sequence is a growing object; growth happens along one axis only.
known_limitations: Frames are always mirror-symmetric rings, so the interior is fully background. Original-style frames with interior decorations are not sampled.
Growing objects never drift perpendicular to their growth axis.
The panel-period and colour-set checks reimplement the described detection locally as constraint filters. Scenes rejected by them are resampled with bounded retries.
The test 2 fixture has two objects with the same colour set that touch the T object diagonally. These are reproduced only through explicit replay parameters; random scenes avoid both features.
Cross-strip dimension is now sampled up to 30; along-strip dimension is at most floor(30/num_panels). This extends panel size, not the mechanism vocabulary.
billing: Claude Max CLI; API credentials excluded; no API fallback
